title: Man, 39, killed in midtown Toronto invasion was musician

blocks.text: Toronto

A man killed in a midtown Toronto home invasion early Wednesday is being remembered as a talented musician who "always led with his heart," according to a longtime friend. Police have identified the man as Michael Eckert, 39.
Michael Eckert was confronted by a suspect before he was shot, police say
Victim in fatal home invasion was Toronto musician
A man killed in a midtown Toronto home invasion early Wednesday is being remembered as a talented musician who "always led with his heart," according to a longtime friend.
Police have identified the man who was fatally shot as Michael Eckert, 39.

Emergency crews responded to reports of a shooting at a residence in the St. Clair Avenue West and Poplar Plains Road area at around 2:40 a.m., according to a Toronto police news release Wednesday afternoon.

An unknown number of suspects forced entry into the residence, police said. One of the suspects was confronted by Eckert, shot him and fled the home, police said. Eckert was taken to hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Staff Sgt. Shain Griffin with 53 Division told CBC News early Wednesday morning the victim was the homeowner's son.
Police identified the victim of a shooting during a home invasion in midtown Toronto Wednesday as Michael Eckert, 39, of Toronto. (Toronto Police Service)
Toronto police Det. Sgt. Alan Bartlett said at a news conference earlier Wednesday that there is no evidence to suggest the family was targeted.
"I understand and recognize how deeply troubling this must be, not only to the residents of that community, but to the residents of the city of Toronto as a whole," Bartlett said.
There were four residents inside the home at the time but no one else was injured, he said.
This is Toronto's 37th homicide of the year, according to police.
Bartlett said Toronto police Chief Myron Demkiw assured him that every resource available will be provided to investigators and "no expense will be spared."
He said police do not yet have details on the number of suspects, any descriptions or what vehicles may have been used.
He urged anyone with surveillance video or anyone who saw anything between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m. to contact police.
Residents on edge after man killed during attempted home invasion
Victim was a 'loving and caring person': friend

Galen Pelley, a friend of Eckert, said he knew him for about 20 years after they met studying music at Humber College. He said they made music together ever since they met and he felt Eckert was like a brother to him.
"We're all still in shock," Pelley said Wednesday. "We can't believe that this would happen to anyone, let alone someone that we all cared about and who cared for so many himself."
Pelley said Eckert, the youngest child in his family, had two sisters and two brothers and did more than his share of taking care of others. He was also an uncle, he said.
"Mike always led with his heart, both on stage and off stage," he said. "He had an affinity for drummers and I always thought guitarists wrote the best songs."
Friend of fatal home invasion victim says Michael was ‘chosen family’
Pelley described Eckert as a "gentle giant" who was an avid reader and a humble, "loving and caring person."
"He spoke louder through his music than he ever would off stage or in person," he said.
Eckert's instrument of choice was the pedal steel guitar, he said.
Eckert performed at the 113th Grey Cup in Calgary as back up for Blue Rodeo this month, Pelley said, adding: "He's gone too soon and that was a real moment for him to flourish."
'Far too many' home invasions in Toronto: city councillor
Coun. Josh Matlow told reporters outside the home Wednesday there have been "far too many" home invasions in the city and that it needs to be a top priority to address residents' concerns.

"There's a feeling amongst Torontonians that far too often people go to bed at night worrying about whether or not they'll wake up to somebody in their home," Matlow said, adding there's work to do in the community to support "very scared" residents.
He said he has offered Demkiw his "complete support" during the investigation. He urged people to not jump to conclusions.
MPP Stephanie Smyth, who joined Matlow, said police do what they can to investigate incidents, but that more needs to be done to address the fear residents feel.

Coun. Josh Matlow and MPP Stephanie Smyth spoke to reporters outside the scene of a fatal home invasion on Wednesday. They shared their condolences for the victim's loved ones and reassured residents they will do their best to address fears. (Paul Smith/CBC)
"They can talk about the stats all they want, but the bottom line is people are afraid. And the one place you should not feel afraid is in your own home," she said.

Matlow added that "it's shameful" to hear that many residents in the neighbourhood and nearby areas have hired private security to safeguard their homes. Smyth said there needs to be stronger deterrence for such crimes, such as harsher penalties.
"People have to do what they feel is the right choice to ensure the safety of their family," Bartlett said in regards to some people hiring private security.

When asked what tips he had for residents regarding a potential home invasion, he said people should call 911 immediately and that Toronto Police Service "provides the best that it can in terms of public safety services."
"Oftentimes we can't provide the why, we simply don't know. What my promise has been to the victims' family is that we'll do our very best to provide the who."
Incident follows Bridle Path home invasion last month

The incident comes nearly a month after a home invasion and shooting sent a family of four adults in Toronto's Bridle Path neighbourhood to hospital. Police arrested one suspect in Ottawa last week and are looking for two others.

Police have been investigating and patrolling to deter home invasions in parts of the city after seeing a rise in incidents earlier this year, Demkiw said in remarks to the Toronto Police Service Board back in July.

Here's where home invasions are happening in Toronto and what's being done to prevent them

blocks.text: He said the service launched the initiative in areas that saw the largest increase in home invasions, which includes 22, 32 and 53 Divisions. The 22 division covers neighbourhoods in central and southern Etobicoke, 32 operates in central and western North York, and 53 Division covers central and midtown Toronto.
"We continue to put our people and our resources where we see challenges, and where we hear concerns from our communities," Demkiw told the police board.

Home invasions hit a 10-year high in 2024, before dropping in 2025 and then rising again at the beginning of this year in Toronto, according to CBC News analysis of Toronto police data. Affluent areas with large detached houses and driveways were among the hardest hit.
